title: Normalization formula for the arithmetic genus of a reduced proper curve
statement:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure] and $X$ a nonempty proper reduced $k$-scheme of pure dimension one [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-pc-reduced-scheme, def-weil-pure-dimension]. Give each irreducible component $X_i$ its reduced induced closed subscheme structure [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme], let $\widetilde X_i	o X_i$ be its normalization [def-sc-normalization], and let $
u:\widetilde X=\coprod_{i=1}^{v}\widetilde X_i	o X$ be their disjoint union. Then $v$ is finite, $
u$ is finite, each $\widetilde X_i$ is a smooth proper connected curve [def-sc-curves], and $F=
u_*\mathcal O_{\widetilde X}/\mathcal O_X$ is supported on finitely many closed points. Write $g_i=\dim_k H^1(\widetilde X_i,\mathcal O_{\widetilde X_i})$ [def-sc-genus] and $\delta_X(y)=\dim_k F_y$ for a closed point $y$. With structure-sheaf cohomology [def-sc-ringed-space-module-cohomology] and $p_a(X)=1-\chi(X,\mathcal O_X)$ [def-pc-euler-characteristic], one has
$$p_a(X)=1-v+\sum_{i=1}^{v}g_i+\sum_{y\in X	ext{ closed}}\delta_X(y).$$
Connectedness and nodality of $X$ are not assumed.

source.place: Appendix B, Lemma B.1 and its normalization exact sequence, printed p. 57; same Euler-characteristic identity for possibly disconnected curves. Primary PDF read online; local archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: Since $X$ is proper over $k$, it is of finite type. The spectrum of a field is Noetherian (its only ideals are zero and the unit ideal), so [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] makes $X$ Noetherian. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-algebraic-normalization-field-change] to the reduced finite-type scheme $X$: its irreducible components form a finite family and their componentwise normalization $\nu$ is finite and surjective. The same node supplies a dense open normal locus $N\subseteq X$ over which $\nu$ is an isomorphism. Each component generic point is in $N$: its reduced local ring has just one prime ideal and is therefore a field.

Each $X_i$ is nonempty, reduced and irreducible, hence integral by [def-pc-integral-scheme]. Its dimension is one by the pure-dimension hypothesis. It is proper over $k$ because it is a closed subscheme of the proper scheme $X$ [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper], and therefore is of finite type. Apply [lem-sc-normalization-properties](a),(c): $\widetilde X_i\to X_i$ is finite, $\widetilde X_i$ is proper, has dimension one, and is smooth since $k$ is perfect. Here perfectness follows directly from algebraic closedness: in positive characteristic every $a\in k$ has a $p$-th root, and in characteristic zero all irreducible polynomials are separable. The proper scheme $X_i$ is separated, hence quasi-separated. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-normalization-in-residue-field-extension] with the generic point of $X_i$ and the degree-one extension $k(X_i)/k(X_i)$; its normalization is exactly the integral-closure construction of [def-sc-normalization], and is integral, hence nonempty and connected. Thus every $\widetilde X_i$ is a smooth proper connected curve.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-finite-curve-quotient-stalk-euler] to $f=\nu$ and the open $N$ from step 1. Its hypotheses are reducedness, properness and pure dimension one of $X$, and finite surjectivity and the isomorphism over $N$, which contains every component generic point by step 1. Writing $B=\nu_*\mathcal O_{\widetilde X}$, it gives the coherent exact sequence $0\to\mathcal O_X\to B\to F\to0$, finite closed support, finite-dimensional stalks, and $\chi(X,F)=\sum_y\delta_X(y)$.

For each $i$, the composite $h_i:\widetilde X_i\to X_i\hookrightarrow X$ is finite: a closed immersion is finite since locally $A/I$ is a cyclic $A$-module [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], and finite maps compose [lem-trf-finite-radicial-basechange]. Apply [lem-trf-finite-smooth-curve-family-euler] to this finite family of smooth proper connected curves. Since its $h$ equals $\nu$ on each summand, it gives $B=\bigoplus_i h_{i,*}\mathcal O_{\widetilde X_i}$ and $\chi(X,B)=v-\sum_i g_i$.

source.place: coherent.tex Tag 089W; varieties.tex Tag 08AA; curves.tex Tag 0BY7. Returned proof steps 8--10.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pc-euler-additive] to the coherent exact sequence of step 3: $\chi(X,\mathcal O_X)=\chi(X,B)-\chi(X,F)=v-\sum_i g_i-\sum_y\delta_X(y)$. Subtract from $1$ and use $p_a(X)=1-\chi(X,\mathcal O_X)$ to obtain the formula. Connectedness and nodality of $X$ were never used.
